Definition: from G575 and G3538; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically):--wash.
BiblicalUsage: Once, and it is Pilate washing his hands. Seeing he could prevail nothing and a tumult was made, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.
TheologicalSignificance: The water washed his hands and nothing else; the guilt stayed exactly where he left it.
